newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares rise on LUKoil, Dow Jones, seen up.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares rise on LUKoil, Dow Jones, seen up.

text.p: Leading Russian shares bounced up in early trade on Monday, despite low volumes, and traders said record gains on Wall Street and first quarter profits posted by oil company LUKoil, were helping to clear last week's lethargy.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index opened at 364.90, barely changed from Friday's closing 364.78.
National power company UES rose to $0.3175 at 0930 GMT from $0.3159 on Friday while LUKoil rose to $16.03 from $15.75.
LUKoil announced first quarter production rose 4.6 percent over the same period in 1996 to 15 million tonnes. It said first quarter net profits rose to 757 billion roubles from 679 billion in 1996.
Aton trader Boris Shvedsky said other leading shares were likely to follow LUKoil, although the Dow Jones' record-breaking performance last week was also fuelling growth.

"It's partially related to the Dow Jones," said Shvedsky. "And people became optimistic and started buying (LUKoil on first quarter 1997 profits) and other "blue chips" are following, although there's not such aggressive buying as in LUKoil."
Oil companies Tatneft and Surgutneftegaz also rose slightly. Tatneft firmed to $90.0 from $87.5 and Surgutneftegaz ticked up to $0.971 from $0.943.
Retail bank Sberbank was also strong, rising to $227 from $214 on Friday.

Rinaco Plus trader Charles Shearer said automobile plants PAZ and UAZ were in demand on the second tier, as well as regional telecoms. He declined to quote a price or bid/offer rates for the companies.
Traders saw the market index closing slightly higher overall by the end of the day, although Shvedsky saw a possible correction in the afternoon.
"I think the index will close higher but...I think maybe Russian brokers will take profits," said Shvedsky.
